name: effect-v4-node-files
body: Use the FileSystem service for filesystem operations. Wrapping Node fs in Effect.sync or Effect.tryPromise does not provide the service abstraction. Keep unavoidable native filesystem code in an excluded adapter.
positive: import fs from "node:fs"; export const read = fs.readFileSync;
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-node-path
body: Use the injected Path service for platform-dependent paths. Preserve explicit POSIX or Windows semantics when they matter; keep platform-specific integration in an adapter.
positive: import path from "node:path"; export const join = path.join;
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-node-http
body: Use the Effect HTTP client for requests and the matching platform adapter at startup. Preserve HTTP status handling, response lifetime, streaming, timeout, and retry semantics.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-node-child-process
body: Use ChildProcess and ChildProcessSpawner from the installed v4 process API. Pass explicit arguments, choose environment inheritance deliberately, and scope subprocess lifetime and output consumption.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-node-timers
body: Use Effect.sleep for waiting, Schedule for recurring work, and Effect retry operations for retries. Keep the original timing and cancellation contract.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-node-streams
body: Use Effect Stream and Sink in business pipelines. Keep Node stream conversion in adapters and preserve backpressure, ordering, early termination, and resource cleanup.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-node-crypto
body: Prefer an equivalent Effect crypto operation; secure UUIDs use SecureRandom from effect/crypto. Preserve algorithm, encoding, and security properties. Put unmatched native crypto operations in an injected adapter.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-obsolete-imports
body: Use the installed Effect v4 exports and migration map. Schema, Match, FileSystem, and Path are integrated in effect; Result replaces the v3 Either module. Verify HTTP and process paths against the lockfile before changing an import.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-foreign-http-clients
body: Prefer the existing Effect HttpClient for business HTTP work. If an existing SDK or required protocol capability needs this client, place it behind an injected adapter and preserve its cancellation and error semantics.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-global-fetch
body: For global HTTP requests, use the injected Effect HttpClient instead of wrapping fetch in a Promise Effect. Decode external bodies, handle status codes deliberately, and preserve cancellation. A local domain function named fetch is not a global HTTP call.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-global-console
body: Use Effect.log operations for application logs and structured context. Intentional human output belongs to Console or Terminal; keep machine-readable output separate. Check whether console is a shadowed local binding before changing it.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-global-timers
body: Use Effect.sleep or Schedule for business timing. Adapt required foreign callbacks outside business code, and preserve fixed-rate versus spaced timing. Check local bindings before replacing a syntactic timer call.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-global-clock
body: Read current time through Clock or the corresponding Effect date/time operation. Preserve wall-clock versus monotonic-time semantics. Pure construction from an existing timestamp can remain a pure conversion.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-global-random
body: Use Random for ordinary business randomness and inject a deterministic source in tests. Security-sensitive values require a cryptographically secure source instead.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-secure-uuid
body: Use the installed v4 SecureRandom service for secure UUID generation. Preserve UUID version and formatting, and provide its required Layer at composition. Never substitute ordinary seeded Random for secure randomness.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-process-env
body: Read application settings through Config and validate them at the boundary. Keep secrets Redacted and replace ConfigProvider in tests. Direct host-environment access belongs to configuration bootstrap adapters.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-native-json
body: Use the appropriate Schema JSON codec at this boundary. Keep parsing failures typed and preserve the wire format, omission behavior, transformations, and numeric semantics; do not replace serialization mechanically.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-promise-fanout
body: Compose Effect work with Effect.all or Effect.forEach. Choose a concurrency bound for growing input and preserve all-versus-settled result semantics. Effect.all and forEach are sequential unless concurrency is configured.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-promise-race
body: Use the Effect race operation matching first completion or first success. Preserve aggregate failure behavior and cancel losing work where the underlying operation supports cancellation.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-new-promise
body: Use Effect composition for business control flow. Bridge foreign callbacks with Effect.callback in an adapter, creating work lazily and registering cleanup. Do not claim interruption cancels a foreign operation that has no cancellation support.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-abort-controller
body: Use the Effect-provided AbortSignal or the signal supplied to a Promise/callback constructor when adapting cancellable work. Keep unavoidable controller ownership in an adapter; do not start an unrelated cancellation tree.
negative: const request = Effect.tryPromise({ try: (signal) => sdk.load({ signal }), catch: toError });
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-process-exit
body: Return a typed outcome from business code. Let the application entry point own exit status, signals, and graceful shutdown through the platform runtime.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-runtime-in-business
body: Compose and yield Effects inside business code instead of starting another runtime. Keep runMain and Promise framework bridges at an explicit application boundary, reusing the intended services and lifetime.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-detached-fiber
body: Check the owner of this background fiber. Prefer child or scoped lifetime for operation-owned work; detached work needs intentional application ownership, failure observation, and shutdown behavior.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-schema-sync
body: In an Effect workflow, use the corresponding Effect-based Schema decode or encode operation so validation failures stay in the typed error channel. Pure synchronous validation at an intentional boundary may remain synchronous.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-native-error-class
body: Use a tagged Data or Schema error for expected domain failures, with useful context. Native Error subclasses needed by a foreign protocol belong in the corresponding adapter; defects may still carry an Error cause.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Type-aware diagnostics handle aliases and shadowed bindings.

name: effect-v4-bun-files
body: Use the FileSystem service instead of Bun.file, Bun.write, Bun.mmap, or Bun.embeddedFiles: readFile, readFileString, writeFile, writeFileString, stream, sink, and open for a scoped file handle. Provide BunFileSystem or BunServices layers at the entry point. Wrapping Bun calls in Effect.promise does not make them a replaceable service.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-glob
body: Replace Bun.Glob with FileSystem.glob for directory scans, or the effect Glob module (Glob.make, Glob.match) for pure pattern matching. Stream or bound large scan results.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-paths
body: Use the Path service instead of Bun.fileURLToPath, Bun.pathToFileURL, Bun.resolve, Bun.resolveSync, or Bun.main: path.fromFileUrl, path.toFileUrl, and path.resolve. Module resolution and entry-file detection belong to the application entry point, not business code.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-stdio
body: Use Terminal (readLine, readInput, display) or Stdio instead of Bun.stdin, Bun.stdout, Bun.stderr, or Bun.Terminal. Use Effect.log for logs and Console for intentional human output. ANSI helpers such as Bun.stringWidth, Bun.stripANSI, Bun.wrapAnsi, and Bun.color belong in effect/cli output or an excluded presentation adapter.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-argv
body: Parse command-line input with effect/cli Command, Flag, and Argument, or read Stdio.args, instead of Bun.argv. Run the command from the entry point with BunRuntime.runMain and pass parsed values into business code.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-env
body: Read settings through Config instead of Bun.env or Bun.secrets. Validate them with Config.schema, keep secrets in Config.Redacted values, and replace the ConfigProvider in tests. Host environment and secret-store access belong to a configuration layer provided at the entry point.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-http-server
body: Define routes with HttpRouter or HttpApi from effect/http and serve them with HttpServer instead of Bun.serve or Bun.FileSystemRouter. Provide BunHttpServer.layer at the entry point. Implement cross-cutting concerns such as CSRF as HttpMiddleware instead of Bun.CSRF, and decode request input with Schema.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-http-client
body: Use the injected HttpClient from effect/http instead of Bun.fetch. Build requests with HttpClientRequest, handle status codes explicitly, decode bodies with Schema, and provide FetchHttpClient.layer or BunHttpClient at the entry point so interruption cancels the request.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Global fetch is reported by effect-v4-global-fetch.

name: effect-v4-bun-cookies
body: Use the Cookies module from effect/http instead of Bun.Cookie or Bun.CookieMap. Read request cookies from HttpServerRequest and set response cookies on HttpServerResponse.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-sockets
body: Use Socket, SocketServer, and DatagramSocket from effect/socket instead of Bun.connect, Bun.listen, Bun.udpSocket, or Bun.udp. Acquire connections in a Scope so they close on interruption, and provide the Bun socket layers at the entry point.
positive: const socket = await Bun.connect({ hostname: "localhost", port: 8080, socket: handlers });
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-dns
body: Resolve names through the Dns service from effect/net instead of Bun.dns so lookups are injectable, interruptible, and replaceable in tests.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-subprocess
body: Use ChildProcess and ChildProcessSpawner from effect/process instead of Bun.spawn, Bun.spawnSync, Bun.$, or Bun.which. Pass explicit argument arrays instead of shell strings, choose environment inheritance deliberately, scope the process lifetime, and consume output as a Stream.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun, including $, are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-time
body: Use Effect.sleep instead of Bun.sleep or Bun.sleepSync, and Clock.currentTimeNanos or Clock.currentTimeMillis instead of Bun.nanoseconds. Clock-based code stays interruptible and controllable with TestClock.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-cron
body: Schedule recurring work with Schedule.cron and the Cron module instead of Bun.cron. Run the schedule in a fiber owned by a Scope or Layer so shutdown stops it.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-password
body: Hash and verify passwords with the Password service from effect/crypto instead of Bun.password. Pass passwords as Redacted values, call needsRehash to upgrade stored hashes, and configure the algorithm in the Password layer.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-hashing
body: Use Digest from effect/crypto (sha256, sha512, digestHex) instead of Bun.CryptoHasher, Bun.sha, or Bun.SHA256-style classes, and Mac for HMAC. Bun.hash is non-cryptographic: use the effect Hash module only for in-memory equality hashing, never for security or persisted identifiers.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-uuid
body: Generate UUIDs with SecureRandom from effect/crypto (uuidV7 or uuidV4) instead of Bun.randomUUIDv7, and provide its layer at the entry point. Bun.randomUUIDv5 derives a deterministic name-based ID: compute it from Digest in a pure helper or adapter.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-sql
body: Use SqlClient from effect/sql instead of Bun.sql, Bun.SQL, Bun.postgres, or bun:sqlite. Provide @effect/sql-sqlite-bun or @effect/sql-pg layers at the entry point, run multi-statement work in withTransaction, and decode rows with SqlSchema.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-redis
body: Use the Redis service from effect/persistence, provided by BunRedis at the entry point, instead of Bun.redis or Bun.RedisClient. For plain caching prefer KeyValueStore or PersistedCache so the backend stays replaceable.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-s3
body: Effect has no built-in S3 client. Define a service for the storage operations business code needs, implement it with Bun.s3 or an SDK in an excluded adapter Layer, map failures to typed errors, and expose object bodies as Stream values.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-streams
body: Use Stream and Sink instead of Bun.readableStreamTo* helpers, Bun.ArrayBufferSink, or Bun.concatArrayBuffers. Convert at the boundary with Stream.fromReadableStream, then use decodeText, mkString, runCollect, or a fitting Sink, bounding how much is collected.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-encoding
body: Parse with effect/encoding modules instead of Bun.TOML, Bun.YAML, Bun.JSON5, Bun.JSONC, Bun.JSONL, or Bun.XML: Toml.parse, Yaml.parse, Json5.parse, Jsonc.parse, Ndjson, and Xml. Then decode the parsed value with a Schema so failures stay typed.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-compression
body: Use Zip or Tar from effect/encoding instead of Bun.Archive, and HttpMiddleware.compression for HTTP responses. Effect has no general gzip, deflate, or zstd module: put Bun compression calls in an injected adapter service with typed errors, because synchronous variants block the fiber.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-data-utils
body: Use Equal.equals instead of Bun.deepEquals or Bun.deepMatch, SemVer and SemVerRange instead of Bun.semver, and Formatter.format instead of Bun.inspect. HTML escaping with Bun.escapeHTML belongs in the rendering adapter.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-runtime-internals
body: Bun runtime and tooling APIs such as Bun.build, Bun.plugin, Bun.Transpiler, Bun.gc, Bun.peek, Bun.unsafe, Bun.version, Bun.WebView, bun:ffi, and bun:jsc do not belong in business code. Keep them in build scripts or the entry point, and pass any needed runtime facts in through Config or a service.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic. Named imports from bun are reported by effect-v4-bun-module.

name: effect-v4-bun-module
body: Importing from bun or reading globalThis.Bun ties business code to the Bun runtime. Use the effect replacement for each API, such as FileSystem, HttpServer, HttpClient, ChildProcess, Config, SqlClient, or SecureRandom, and provide Bun implementations with @effect/platform-bun layers at the entry point.
limitation: AST matching is syntactic and does not cover bun:test. Type-only imports from bun also match.
